arxiv-2210-00287.title: Spherically symmetric, static black holes with scalar hair, and naked singularities in nonminimally coupled k-essence
arxiv-2210-00287.creator: Cecília Nagy, Zoltán Keresztes, László Á. Gergely
arxiv-2210-00287.description: Abstract We apply a recently developed 2+1+1 decomposition of spacetime, based on a nonorthogonal double foliation for the study of spherically symmetric, static black hole solutions of Horndeski scalar-tensor theory. Our discussion proceeds in an effective field theory (EFT) of modified gravity approach, with the action depending on metric and embedding scalars adapted to the nonorthogonal 2+1+1 decomposition.

arxiv-2311-08470.title: Searching for the Imprints of AGN Feedback on the Lyman Alpha Forest Around Luminous Red Galaxies 2023 Searching for the Imprints of AGN Feedback on the Lyman Alpha Forest Around Luminous Red Galaxies – 14
arxiv-2311-08470.creator: Vikram Khaire, Teng Hu, Joseph F. Hennawi, Joseph N. Burchett, Michael Walther and Frederick Davies
arxiv-2311-08470.description: Abstract We explore the potential of using the low-redshift Lyman- α \alpha (Ly α \alpha ) forest surrounding luminous red galaxies (LRGs) as a tool to constrain active galactic nuclei (AGN) feedback models. Our analysis is based on snapshots from the Illustris and IllustrisTNG simulations at a redshift of z = 0.1 z=0.1 .

arxiv-2412-17571.title: HPCNeuroNet: A Neuromorphic Approach Merging SNN Temporal Dynamics with Transformer Attention for FPGA-based Particle Physics
arxiv-2412-17571.creator: \firstname Murat \lastname Isik, \firstname Hiruna \lastname Vishwamith, \firstname Jonathan \lastname Naoukin, \firstname I. Can \lastname Dikmen
arxiv-2412-17571.description: Abstract This paper presents the innovative HPCNeuroNet model, a pioneering fusion of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), Transformers, and high-performance computing tailored for particle physics, particularly in particle identification from detector responses. Our approach leverages SNNs’ intrinsic temporal dynamics and Transformers’ robust attention mechanisms to enhance performance when discerning intricate particle interactions.

pmc-10528232.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Synthetic Peptides Based on Glucocorticoid-Induced Leucine Zipper (GILZ) Protein for the Treatment of Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IBDs)
pmc-10528232.creator: Musetta Paglialunga, Sara Flamini, Raffaele Contini, Marta Febo, Erika Ricci, Simona Ronchetti, Oxana Bereshchenko, Graziella Migliorati, Carlo Riccardi, Stefano Bruscoli
pmc-10528232.description: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are commonly used to treat autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, but their clinical effects and long-term use can lead to serious side effects. New drugs that can replace GCs are needed. Glucocorticoid-induced leucine zipper (GILZ) is induced by GCs and mediates many of their anti-inflammatory effects, such as inhibiting the pro-inflammatory molecule NF-κB.

pmc-11431122.title: Evaluating Access to Health Care in Mothers and Caregivers of Children under Five Years of Age in Rural Communities of Yucatán, Mexico
pmc-11431122.creator: Elsa Rodríguez, Guadalupe Andueza, Ricardo Ojeda, Erin Palmisano, Louisa Ewald, Aruna M. Kamath, Abraham Flaxman, Shwetha H. Sanapoori, Bernardo Hernandez
pmc-11431122.description: Populations in rural communities have more limited access to health care and attention than urban populations. The present study aimed to evaluate barriers to access to health care in mothers and caregivers of children under five years of age, twelve months after an educational intervention.

pmc-11591747.title: Simulation of a Bio-Inspired Flocking-Based Aggregation Behaviour in Swarm Robotics
pmc-11591747.creator: Samira Rasouli, Kerstin Dautenhahn, Chrystopher L Nehaniv, Heming Jia
pmc-11591747.description: This paper presents a biologically inspired flocking-based aggregation behaviour of a swarm of mobile robots. Aggregation behaviour is essential to many swarm systems, such as swarm robotics systems, in order to accomplish complex tasks that are impossible for a single agent.

pmc-12589705.title: Trehalose 6‐phosphate – a central regulator at the crossroads of sugar signalling, metabolism, and development
pmc-12589705.creator: Franziska Fichtner
pmc-12589705.description: SummaryIn mammals, blood sugar levels are tightly controlled by two hormones: insulin and glucagon. In flowering plants, a comparable regulatory mechanism exists, mediated by the sugar‐signalling molecule trehalose 6‐phosphate (Tre6P). Similar to insulin, Tre6P functions as a signal and negative feedback regulator of sucrose, the main transport sugar in vascular plants.

pmc-12973469.title: LINC00852 inhibits colorectal cancer progression by regulating cell apoptosis, epithelial‒mesenchymal transition, invasion, and cuproptosis through miR-1276/LACTB
pmc-12973469.creator: Chun-Xiao Wang, Xiao-Jing Chen, Ling Zeng, Wang-Wu Liu, Jia-Sheng Ke, Yu-Ze Wu, Xian Deng, Yi Qiu, Ming-Liang Chen, Zhong-Shi Hong, Cheng-Zhi Qiu
pmc-12973469.description: Exploring the role of key genes in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression to identify effective targets is highly practical. Previous studies have shown that miR-1276/ACTB plays an important regulatory role in CRC. In addition to miRNA, lncRNA also play a crucial role in tumour progression. However, there are currently no studies exploring the relationship between lncRNAs and miR-1276/LACTB.

pmc-13043697.title: Blunt-force assembly of programmable DNA architectures using π–π stacking
pmc-13043697.creator: Karol Woloszyn, Andrew Horvath, Mara Jaffe, Lara Perren, Joe Rueb, Samyra Mahiba, Nataša Jonoska, Yoel P Ohayon, James W Canary, Simon Vecchioni, Ruojie Sha
pmc-13043697.description: Sticky-ended cohesion has been the driving force for DNA self-assembly and has enabled model and design programmability in DNA nanotechnology for over 40 years. Traditional units within self-assembled crystals have rationally-designed sticky ends to avoid unpredictable packing behavior, but in doing so, the surprising variety of contact flavors available to natural nucleic acids remains unexploited.

pmc-13120301.title: Comparative Analysis of Abattoir-Based Measures and On-Farm Pig Welfare Indicators in Italian Fattening Heavy Pigs
pmc-13120301.creator: Lucia Scuri, Matteo Recchia, Federico Scali, Claudia Romeo, Antonio Marco Maisano, Giovanni Santucci, Camilla Allegri, Marta Masserdotti, Miriam Tenuzzo, Adriana Ianieri, Sergio Ghidini, Giovanni Loris Alborali
pmc-13120301.description: Simple SummaryOn-farm evaluations provide direct insight into animal welfare, but they are costly and time-consuming. Assessing key indicators (e.g., tail, skin and ear lesions) at the abattoir improves efficiency by centralising the examination of pigs from multiple farms. However, agreement between these methods remains underexplored, particularly in heavy pig production (160–170 kg).

pmc-13295515.title: Effects of Flat-Side Design on Torsional and Bending Stress of Nickel–Titanium File by Finite Element Analysis
pmc-13295515.creator: Yinjie Yang, Xinfang Cao, Jiwu Zhang, Yuqing Zhou, Songhao Chen, Benxiang Hou
pmc-13295515.description: Background: This study evaluated the effects of flattening the side of the bending resistance and torsional resistance of nickel–titanium files through finite element analysis of a novel flattened file and a standard nonflattened file. Methods: For torsion analysis, the tip of the file was fixed at 3 mm, generating a torque of 2.5 N·mm at the handle.

pmc-13353424.title: A scalable deep-learning framework for cancer detection using cell-free DNA shallow whole-genome sequencing
pmc-13353424.creator: Haichao Wang, Paulius D. Mennea, Grainne McAndrew, Ozge Sonmezler, Dmitry S. Shcherbo, Emma-Jane Ditter, Sarah Østrup Jensen, Alessandra I. G. Buma, Christopher G. Smith, Zhao Cheng, Clare Harris, Rosalind. J. Cutts, Sarah Hrebien, Philip A. J. Crosbie, Pippa G. Corrie, Michel M. van den Heuvel, Ami
pmc-13353424.description: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in body fluids enables noninvasive cancer detection. Multifeature artificial intelligence (AI) can improve sensitivity by integrating diverse biomarkers when cancer signals are sparse. Tumor-informed assays that rely on mutations have limited practicality for early cancer detection. Emerging fragmentomic and epigenetic features underpin tumor-naive approaches to screening for individuals with low tumor burden.
